units.text: Motivation: limitations of vanilla SSMs – they ignore irregular timespans and are vulnerable to input noise
Two limitations of vanilla state-space models when applied to dynamic graphs motivate the design that follows.

First, standard SSMs assume uniform timesteps and therefore ignore the irregular timespans that characterize real-world interaction sequences; second, the state update in a vanilla SSM lacks an explicit mechanism to suppress unreliable or noisy transitions, leaving the model vulnerable to input noise.
